items.headline: Balakrishnan says Singapore must be able to say 'no' to both the US and China
items.summary: Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan told the Milken Institute Asia Summit that Singapore has reached a 'peculiarly sensitive existential point' and must keep the ability to refuse both Washington and Beijing to preserve their trust.

items.headline: Ministerial pay benchmarks rise 60% as the PM's climbs to S$3.6 million from October 15
items.summary: Singapore's ministerial salary benchmarks rise about 60% on 15 October, lifting the prime minister's benchmark to S$3.6 million from S$2.2 million. PM Lawrence Wong will donate his roughly S$1.4 million increase to charity over five years.

items.headline: Update: Indonesian haze keeps Singapore's air in the unhealthy band as Malaysia shuts schools
items.summary: Transboundary haze from fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan pushed Singapore's air pollution to among the worst in the world this week, with the NEA rating all regions unhealthy and Malaysia ordering schools in affected districts to close.

items.headline: Singaporean massage-parlour boss becomes third on a US 'worst criminal aliens' list
items.summary: Jing Emtage, a 54-year-old Singaporean, was added to the US DHS 'worst of the worst' criminal aliens list after a conviction over a prostitution ring run through massage parlours in Washington state; 23 trafficked women were rescued.

items.headline: India calls US Vice-President Vance's 'indentured servants' remark deeply offensive
items.summary: India's foreign ministry called remarks by US VP JD Vance 'deeply offensive' after he said companies were replacing laid-off Americans with 'foreign indentured servants', saying the words carried painful colonial connotations.

items.headline: US suspends Microsoft, Adobe and top Indian IT firms from a green-card labour programme
items.summary: The US Labor Department suspended Microsoft, Adobe and major Indian IT companies including Infosys and TCS from the PERM green-card programme over alleged visa abuse; India said existing H-1B visas are unaffected.

items.headline: Update: India's 'cockroach' movement says 10,000 detained as election-chief protests spread
items.summary: The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party and opposition parties said about 10,000 people have been detained nationwide in protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over voter-roll revisions.

items.headline: India's Supreme Court agrees to hear challenges to the Election Commission's voter-roll revision
items.summary: India's Supreme Court agreed to take up petitions challenging the Election Commission's nationwide voter-roll revision and the conduct of its chief, after the commission reported removing more than 130 million names.

items.headline: Update: Labour holds Starmer's old Holborn and St Pancras seat, beating the Greens
items.summary: Labour's Sagal Abdi-Wali won the Holborn and St Pancras by-election with 12,292 votes to Green leader Zack Polanski's 8,928, a majority of about 3,360, in the seat vacated by former PM Keir Starmer.

items.headline: Greens' Zack Polanski vows to stay on as leader after the by-election defeat
items.summary: Green leader Zack Polanski, beaten into second place with almost a third of the vote, said he would stay on as leader amid questions about his leadership and slipping personal poll ratings.

items.headline: Burnham pledges to ban non-compete clauses for startups ahead of the October Budget
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham said his government will legislate to stop non-compete clauses blocking hiring at startups and scaling firms, calling it 'needed and long overdue'; detail is expected in the 28 October Budget.

items.headline: Britain's Green Party classes Zionism as a form of racism, drawing cross-party criticism
items.summary: A Green Party conference motion classifying Zionism as a form of racism continued to shadow the by-election campaign, drawing criticism from Jewish groups, rival parties and many Green lawmakers; leader Zack Polanski did not vote on it.

items.headline: Navi Pillay, former UN rights chief, wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
items.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, the South African jurist and former UN human-rights chief, citing her efforts for peace and international law; she recently led the UN commission that found genocide in Gaza.

items.headline: Ukraine pushes Russia back in Donetsk as military and civilian casualties climb
items.summary: Ukrainian forces reported pushing Russian troops back in parts of Donetsk even as casualties mounted along the front, days after a Russian strike on buses in Kramatorsk killed dozens.

items.headline: Gaza ceasefire 'exists in name only', more than 100 aid groups say one year on
items.summary: More than 100 humanitarian and rights organisations said the Gaza ceasefire exists only on paper a year after it began, citing Gaza Health Ministry figures of more than 1,470 Palestinians killed since the truce.

items.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guard strikes a gas tanker near Hormuz as attacks hit Riyadh's airport
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it struck a large LPG tanker near the Strait of Hormuz as the US-Iran conflict intensified, while two attacks on Riyadh's King Khalid airport killed three people.

items.headline: China's Manus raises over $500 million in its first round since the Meta split
items.summary: Butterfly Effect, maker of AI agent Manus, said it raised more than $500 million led by Boyu Capital and IDG Capital, its first round since Meta called off a reported $2 billion acquisition; it recently launched Manus 2.0.

items.headline: Waymo locks in a $5 billion loan from Blackstone and PIMCO to expand its robotaxis
items.summary: Waymo closed a $5 billion loan from lenders including PIMCO, Blackstone and Sixth Street to fund robotaxi expansion; the Alphabet unit now runs paid services in 15 markets and is testing in London and Tokyo.

items.headline: Uber and China's Pony.ai plan to launch robotaxis in London
items.summary: Uber and Chinese autonomous-driving firm Pony.ai said they plan a robotaxi service in London, with testing of Pony.ai's Gen-7 vehicles to begin in the coming weeks.

items.headline: Cal AI's 19-year-old founder raises $10 million for a personal-AI startup, Persona
items.summary: Zach Yadegari, 19-year-old co-founder of Cal AI, raised $10 million led by Vine Ventures for a new personal-AI startup, Persona, which plans a wearable band priced at around $179.

items.headline: Wall Street climbs into earnings season as the S&P 500 ends the week at 7,811
items.summary: US stocks rose Friday to cap a volatile week, with the S&P 500 up 0.59% to 7,811.54, the Dow up 0.83% to 51,654.95 and the Nasdaq up 0.64% to 27,366.17; all three posted weekly gains.

items.headline: Treasury yields hold near 24-year highs as traders close a volatile week
items.summary: Longer-dated US Treasury yields held near multi-decade highs as traders wrapped up a choppy week, with the 10-year yield around 5.24%, reflecting sticky-inflation worries after the Fed's recent rate rise.

items.headline: Oil climbs as reports say the White House is weighing Iran strike options before the midterms
items.summary: Oil rose, with Brent above $105 a barrel intraday, after reports the White House had asked the Pentagon to prepare options for strikes on Iran before the US midterms; Brent settled near $104.72 on Friday.

items.headline: Starbucks has explored a takeover of Chipotle, the Financial Times reports
items.summary: Starbucks looked into acquiring Chipotle, valued at about $39 billion, in what would rank among the largest restaurant deals on record, per the Financial Times; analysts flagged the price and Starbucks' turnaround as hurdles.

items.headline: Verstappen beats Russell to pole for Singapore's first F1 sprint; Antonelli only seventh
items.summary: Max Verstappen took pole for Formula 1's first Singapore Sprint, edging George Russell with Charles Leclerc third; championship leader Kimi Antonelli starts seventh, 84 points ahead of Russell with seven rounds left.

items.headline: Stewards clear Verstappen over a yellow-flag incident, letting him keep sprint pole
items.summary: F1 stewards investigated Verstappen for passing Lewis Hamilton under yellow flags in sprint qualifying but let his pole stand, accepting the overtake as an unavoidable consequence of the conditions.

items.headline: Hurkacz stuns China Open champion Djokovic in the Shanghai Masters second round
items.summary: Hubert Hurkacz beat Novak Djokovic 6-4, 6-3 in 87 minutes in the Shanghai Masters second round, days after Djokovic won the China Open for his 102nd tour-level title; it was Hurkacz's first win in nine meetings.

items.headline: Shai Hope's unbeaten 102 lifts West Indies to level the India T20I series 1-1
items.summary: Shai Hope made an unbeaten 102 off 45 balls and Sherfane Rutherford 84 as West Indies chased 250 in Ranchi to beat India by six wickets and level the five-match T20I series 1-1; Sanju Samson made 82 for India.

items.headline: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 splashes down off California after nearly eight months in orbit
items.summary: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 splashed down off California on 8 October after nearly eight months on the ISS, carrying NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA's Sophie Adenot and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev.

items.headline: Big dogs age faster than small ones, and 'jumping genes' may be to blame
items.summary: A study of nearly 900 dogs across about 120 breeds found larger dogs accumulate age-related DNA changes faster than smaller ones; researchers point to mobile 'jumping genes' as a possible driver, though that link is still a hypothesis.

items.headline: NASA releases the first science data and images from its Artemis II lunar flyby
items.summary: NASA published the first tranche of science data and imagery gathered during Artemis II, its crewed mission around the Moon, adding the material to a public archive to help prepare for future lunar-surface missions.

items.headline: NASA says Arctic sea ice hit its 2026 minimum, the 10th-lowest in the satellite record
items.summary: NASA and the NSIDC reported Arctic sea ice reached its 2026 summer minimum of about 4.6 million square kilometres on 12 September, tying for the 10th-lowest in the satellite record; remaining ice is younger and thinner.

fun_fact.headline: A day on Venus is longer than its year
fun_fact.body: A day on Venus is longer than its year. The planet takes about 243 Earth days to spin once on its axis but only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun. Venus also rotates backwards compared with most planets, so from its surface the Sun would rise in the west and set in the east.

puzzle.title: Photo Finish
puzzle.body: Four friends — Ava, Ben, Cora, and Dan — finished a race in positions 1st to 4th, with no ties. Ava finished ahead of Ben; Cora was neither first nor last; Dan finished immediately behind Cora; Ben did not finish last. In what order did they finish?
puzzle.approach: Pin down the one runner whose place is boxed in by two clues, then let the rest fall into line.
puzzle.answer: 1st Ava, 2nd Ben, 3rd Cora, 4th Dan. Cora must be 2nd or 3rd; if 2nd, Dan is 3rd and Ben would have to be 1st (not last) with Ava 4th, breaking 'Ava ahead of Ben'. So Cora is 3rd, Dan 4th, Ava 1st, Ben 2nd.

word_puzzle.title: More or Less
word_puzzle.body: Turn MORE into LESS in exactly four steps, changing one letter at a time and keeping a real word each step.
word_puzzle.approach: Change one letter at each step, keeping a real word every time, until the word becomes its own opposite.
